title: Cranial Avocado Ballistics Lab
description: A stone bust of a human head (LeePerrySmith) sits on a pedestal in a physics lab. The user operates an avocado cannon, adjusting launch angle, power, spin rate, and gravity to strike specific target zones marked on the head. Avocados follow realistic projectile trajectories with air drag and bounce off the head using collision physics.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with ES modules from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a projectile physics sandbox. Load LeePerrySmith.glb scaled to roughly 3 units tall, centered at origin on a flat pedestal (BoxGeometry). Load Avocado.glb scaled to about 0.4 units as the projectile template. Place the camera at (0, 2, 8) looking at the head with OrbitControls.

Add a visible cannon apparatus (CylinderGeometry) at position (-5, 1, 0) that rotates to show aim direction. Create an HTML overlay control panel with: (1) Launch Angle slider 0-80 degrees, (2) Power slider 1-20 m/s, (3) Spin Rate slider 0-50 rad/s affecting Magnus force, (4) Gravity multiplier slider 0.1-3.0, (5) Air Drag coefficient slider 0-0.5, and (6) a Fire button.

Mark 3 glowing target zones on the head (forehead, nose, chin) using small semi-transparent SphereGeometry with emissive materials. Display a scoreboard tracking hits per zone.

When Fire is pressed, clone the Avocado model and launch it from the cannon tip. Each frame, update velocity using: gravity (adjustable g * multiplier downward), quadratic air drag (−drag * |v| * v), and Magnus force (spin cross velocity vector scaled by coefficient). Rotate the avocado around its velocity axis proportional to spin rate.

Implement collision detection: use a bounding sphere around the head (radius ~1.5). When an avocado enters this sphere, check distance to each target zone center. If within 0.5 units of a target, register a hit with a particle burst (Points with randomized velocities that fade), increment that zone's score, and remove the avocado. Otherwise, apply a bounce reflection off the sphere normal with 0.3 restitution coefficient. Avocados that fall below y=-2 are removed. Limit active avocados to 5.

Add directional light from (5,10,5), ambient light intensity 0.4, and a GridHelper on the ground plane. Include a trajectory preview line (dashed Line) that updates in real-time as sliders change, simulating 100 steps of the trajectory without drag to give an approximate aim guide. Use three distinct colors for the target zone markers and their corresponding score displays.
